scenario.title: Operation Torch
intro.text:
OPERATION TORCH - 24 AUG 1949

East of Mt Grammos, Pindus Mountains

We are on the verge of winning the war! The defeated rebels have been entrenched in the mountains at the Albania border and the General Staff has ordered a last major operation in order to complete our victory. The Americans have supplied us with modern dive bomber and they should help to destroy the strong fortifications. Chase off the remaining communist troops from their fortifications in the Grammos mountains!

GOAL Capture all VH!
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-19-0-briliant.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.reaction-19-0-briliant.text: The Vitsi objectives fell before the DSE could transfer its main force. Headquarters is planning the final operation. I've asked it to wait for our ammunition and casualty returns before setting the date.
line.reaction-19-1-victory-tactical.text: We took the towns, but detachments got away into the high massifs. Ask the patrols where they went. We'll be meeting them again in the next operation.
line.callback-0.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.callback-0.text: The communiqué named the captured towns. Our patrol reports also show where the DSE detachments went afterward. Make sure both reach the planning staff.
line.callback-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.callback-1.text: Closing the routes trapped more DSE men. It also brought search parties into the villages at night. Some of the complaints are about our units. I'll take them to the officers concerned.
line.callback-2.speaker: Thrasyvoulos Tsakalotos
line.callback-2.text: The Konitsa scouts knew the tracks when they reached Vitsi. Keep their guides with them for this operation; I don't want the battalions borrowing men without asking.
line.callback-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.callback-3.text: The Konitsa guides are serving separate units now. Ask those units for their route reports. There isn't a troop headquarters to collect them for us anymore.
line.athens-control-debt.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.athens-control-debt.text: Hale wrote last month. We're using American matériel where we once relied on British supplies. He says the requests attached to the crates sound familiar. I haven't decided how to answer him.
line.athens-corridor-debt.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.athens-corridor-debt.text: Markou sent the names of three families who crossed our Athens corridors. She also sent the names of two men later taken from their homes. She did not add a conclusion for us.
line.scene-0.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.scene-0.text: We possess the superiority we lacked in every earlier year: men, aircraft, guns, and an open supply line. I intend to use it once and finish this.
line.scene-1.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.scene-1.text: Prisoner leaflets are already blowing back across our positions. They promise fair treatment. The local police have added names in pencil beside the promise.
line.scene-2.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.scene-2.text: Then remove the pencils and discipline the police. Do not confuse misconduct with an argument for leaving the DSE an army.
line.scene-3.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.scene-3.text: The operational question remains. Seal every exit and destroy the formations, or leave controlled corridors for surrender and assign troops to protect them from both sides.
line.decision.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.decision.text: Commander, do we close every exit, or assign troops to protect surrender corridors? Once the assault begins, the local officers must know which order applies.
line.decision.choice.close-the-ring.text: Close the ring and commit every gun to destroying organised resistance.
line.decision.choice.close-the-ring.hint: Give infantry and artillery 20 experience and restore the core to at least nine strength with full fuel and ammunition.
line.decision.choice.offer-surrender-cor: Publish surrender guarantees and keep controlled corridors open.
Spend 150 prestige and restore the core to full strength with full fuel and ammunition.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-a-0.text: Close the ring, then. Some men across it will hear artillery and decide the border is kinder than surrender. We should at least know why they ran.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-a-1.text: Air and artillery deny movement; ground forces close by phase. No secondary missions, no local bargains, no gaps left for another season of war.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Alexandros Papagos
line.choice-b-0.text: Corridors consume combat strength and offer the enemy another route to deceive us. I accept them because you will command them, not because I trust the slogans on the leaflets.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Dimitris Laskaris
line.choice-b-1.text: Terms go by radio and leaflet. Units on the corridors answer to military law; prisoners are registered before local authorities touch them. Manesis, choose the sergeants.
line.choice-b-2.speaker: Petros Manesis
line.choice-b-2.text: I already have. They are the ones least eager for the job.
epilogue.government-control-ring-success: Papagos has announced that organised resistance is over. I still have the surrender map here and two cabinets of names to check. In Athens I argued that we could not fight Britain without ruining the army and risking a wider war. I stand by that. But when the prisoners' families come, it won't answer what they ask me.
epilogue.government-corridors-ring-succe: Three families below Grammos remembered the Athens corridors. One asked me to look for a son; we passed him in a prison column an hour later. Your army has won. You kept it out of a war with Britain. Now I need your help finding out where that column was sent.
epilogue.government-control-surrender-su: The corridor brought in fighters without rifles and wounded men on doors. I'm glad we kept it open. We stayed under British command in Athens because I feared we'd lose the army and draw Greece into a wider war. We got through that. I've signed the prisoner register here; I want to know who takes responsibility for these men after us.
epilogue.government-corridors-surrender-: The surrender-post sergeants have brought their registers. Every man is named; no unrecorded handovers. We kept the Athens corridors and opened these too. I'll keep the copies, Commander. The police will be asking for prisoners tomorrow, and I want the receiving officer's signature for each one.
Formations escaped through the gaps and our casualty reports are still coming in. We failed to close the ring. I used to argue that staying with British command would preserve an army for decisions of our own. We had that army here. These orders were ours. I will sign the account of what went wrong.
epilogue.government-corridors-ring-defea: We lost the encirclement, and search parties are entering the villages. People who used the Athens corridors have asked me whether you will protect them here too. I told them I'd bring their names to you. The war is continuing; they need an answer before the next patrol arrives.
epilogue.government-control-surrender-de: The surrender loudspeakers are back on the trucks. Few men heard them before our attack failed. We preserved the brigade in exile and under British command; I wanted it available for a Greek decision. This was one. I approved the plan, and I need to hear from the battalions it cost us.
epilogue.government-corridors-surrender-: We brought back wounded from both sides through the corridor and lost the ground beyond it. Headquarters calls that a failure, which is fair. The men ask whether the war would be over if we had been less careful. I told them I did not know. It is the first honest answer I have given them in some time.
